messages.author: 4f494c3ae8062847
messages.subject: dplyr arrange kills RStudio session
parts:
While trying to arrange a tbl_df with dplyr, RStudio stops running. A Windows notification pop up says "RStudio R session has stopped working" and tries to find a reason. After that,  an RStudio pop up announces "R Session Aborted. R encountered a fatal error. The session was terminated" with a button to re-start R.

My script:
library(dplyr)
dca<-read.table("C:/Users/Norman/Desktop/cap/Daily Charge Anal 2011-2013.CSV", header=TRUE, sep=";")
dca_df<-tbl_df(dca)
dca_df2<-select(dca_df, 6,7,8,12)
names(dca_df2)<-c("dos","voucher","code","fee")
dca_df2$fee<-as.integer(as.character(dca_df2$fee))
dca_df2$dos<-as.Date(dca_df2$dos, format="%m/%d/%Y")
voucher_df<-group_by(dca_df2,voucher,dos)
voucher_df2<-summarise(voucher_df, total=sum(fee))
voucher_by_dos<-arrange(voucher_df2, dos)


Has anybody else run in to this or is it a size/memory issue?

 voucher_df2 is >20k rows by 3 variables

Hmmm, I can't recreate this bug on my machine (also
x86_64-apple-darwin10.8.0). I wonder if it might be because I'm using
clang?

If you would mind spending a little more time on the problem, it would
be great if you could reduce the example still further. These are the
things I'd start with:

* Does it still occur without the intermediate summarise step? If so,
then save that csv and use that as a starting point. If not, remove
the group_by and summary lines.

* Can you isolate the problem to a row or a handful of rows? I'd use a
binary search to do this, dividing the dataset into half each time,
eliminating the half which doesn't cause the bug.

Hadley
